nodes.text: We say that $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is an essential component if $d_s(A+B)>d_s(B)$ for every $B\subset \mathbb{N}$ with $0<d_s(B)<1$ where $d_s$ is the Schnirelmann density . Can a lacunary set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an essential component?

#37 : [Er56,p.136] [Er61,p.229] [Er73,p.135] [ErGr80,p.49] number theory | additive combinatorics The answer is no by Ruzsa [Ru87] , who proved that if $A$ is an essential component then there exists some constant $c>0$ such that $\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \geq (\log N)^{1+c}$ for all large $N$. Furthermore, Ruzsa proves that this is best possible, in that for any $c>0$ there exists an essential component $A$ for which $\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \leq (\log N)^{1+c}$ for all large $N$. See also [1146] for whether $\{2^m3^n\}$ is an essential component.
